comparison_note: These three numbers measure different things and must not be ranked as a single leaderboard. AutoML was scored on a clean held-out TEST set (n=471) with annotation-derived labels. Gemini and OpenCV were scored for agreement with WEAK labels (heuristic box/door presence), which are a noisy proxy, not ground truth. Gemini's SOP verdict is additionally a richer task (7 quality categories + rationale), not just binary package_visible.
method: Structured SOP prompt via Vertex AI (application default credentials, no API key). 114 Open Images validation photos, same set as the OpenCV baselines.
model_note: gemini-2.0-flash and gemini-2.0-flash-001 both returned 404 'publisher model not found' on Vertex AI us-central1 (retired/unavailable); 2.5-flash substituted after a verified test call. Documented, not hidden.

opencv_baseline_vs_same_weak_labels.note: OpenCV heuristic (blur>50 and brightness>25) is permissive: predicted positive on 101/114 images.

weak_labels.description: 89 box/weak-positive, 25 neg/weak-negative; heuristic, not ground truth
